A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EXP-KL-MS research. Text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across the reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 contains theoretical guarantees and proofs, including its appendices. Its tables describe analytical properties and distribution families; no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis results are reported.

after.justification: V2 remains entirely theoretical. Its revised guarantees and additional proofs do not constitute empirical results, and neither the main text nor appendices report experiments or simulations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same initialization, KL-weighted arm sampling and empirical-mean updates. The temperature choices L(k)=k-1, k/d and k already appear in v1; v2 revises their analysis rather than their procedures.

E1.justification: Neither version uses training or evaluation datasets or reports empirical task coverage. Revisions to admissible distribution families concern theoretical assumptions.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same theoretical comparator set, including TS, ExpTS variants, kl-UCB and kl-UCB++. Neither version adds an experimentally evaluated comparison method.

E3.justification: Neither version reports empirical evaluation protocols, dataset splits, experimental sample sizes, training budgets or testing procedures.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablation, robustness or case-study experiments. Both analyze the same temperature variants; their changed mathematical guarantees are assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The concentration inequalities belong to the theoretical analysis.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added, removed or revised. Table 1's theoretical-property entries remain unchanged; changes to analytical regret bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V2 Corollary 5 replaces v1 Corollary 2's additive K ln(T) term with a sum of arm gaps. For L(k)=k, v2 Corollary 12 changes the reported minimax factor from ln(T) to sqrt(ln(T)) and the additive term from K ln(T)^2 to K ln(T); Corollary 13 and Appendix C.2.2 add a Sub-UCB guarantee and proof. Assumption 4's instance interval becomes Assumption 8's bounded-mean interval (0,M], with corresponding Table 2 restrictions. Supporting derivations also change substantially, including Lemma 23's exponential factors and the geometric-log lemma's constant from 3 to 5.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains an OPED bandit algorithm combining asymptotic optimality, a sqrt(ln(K)) minimax factor, Sub-UCB and variance adaptivity. V2 explicitly names the minimax factor in its abstract, but v1 already states it in the introduction.

C2.justification: V1 suggests that refined analysis might establish constant minimax optimality; v2 Section 5 conjectures that sqrt(ln(K)) is tight for the existing algorithm. Section 6 adds an exponential-reward example motivating a conjectured intrinsic obstacle to asymptotic optimality when L(k)=k. V2 also explains restrictions needed for unbounded-variance families.

D1.justification: The algorithmic pseudocode and temperature choices are retained. No implementation settings, hardware or runtime information, or code/data access instructions are introduced.

R1.justification: V2 adds Lee et al. (2021) when discussing linear-bandit extensions. It also qualifies prior-work statements: kl-UCB++ changes from failing adaptive variance to having an unknown guarantee, while ExpTS variants are described as lacking an analysis. Most other bibliography changes consolidate duplicate references or change citation presentation.

P1.justification: The main text and appendix explanations are extensively rewritten. Guarantee definitions move from the introduction into Related Work, Extensions moves into Appendix A, and proofs receive reorganized subsections and a contents listing. Terminology, theorem references and the title spelling are also edited.

P2.justification: A document-wide template change alters the title and author block, typography, running headers, equation formatting and figure placement. Table 2 removes its separate variance-function column and expands its caption. Existing proof diagrams are resized and relabelled, and a contents listing is added.

improvement.justification: V2 improves organization, clarifies variance restrictions and repairs parts of the auxiliary arguments. However, its stronger L(k)=k guarantees have newly inconsistent supporting equations: v1 Equation (27) multiplies by a decaying exponential, whereas v2 Equation (25) and Lemma 23 divide by that factor before Proposition 22 invokes a decaying-series bound. These proof inconsistencies prevent a reliable net quality judgment despite the explanatory and analytical gains.
